cards.explanation: The answer is: Are You for us or for our enemies. Joshua, Israel's leader, asks, “Are You for us or for our enemies?” (Joshua 5:13) He sees a drawn sword and walks UP to it. Me, I'd have asked that question from two counties over, with a megaphone.

The answer is False. The man with the sword does not say He's on Israel's side. Joshua asks if the man is for Israel or for their enemies, and gets one word: “Neither,” (Joshua 5:14). Then the man says, “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.” One word, and the whole question gets turned around. I think Joshua stood there a second just taking that in.

The answer is Commander of the LORD's army. The man says, “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.” (Joshua 5:14) Joshua responds by falling facedown in reverence. Then he asks, “What does my Lord have to say to His servant?” He knows exactly who he's talking to.

The answer is that He tells Joshua to take off his sandals. The Commander says, “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.” (Joshua 5:15) Then the text says, “And Joshua did so.” The order and the obeying sit right next to each other. Sandals off, and that's the whole scene.

The answer is False. Those gates are not swinging open, friends. Joshua 6:1 says, “Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.” Nobody's coming, nobody's going, and nobody's popping out for a quick errand.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Behold, I have delivered Jericho into your hand, along with its king and its mighty men of valor.” (Joshua 6:2) The marching directions don't come until the next verse. The LORD hands Joshua the good news before the first lap even starts.

The answer is once. The LORD says, “March around the city with all the men of war, circling the city one time. Do this for six days.” (Joshua 6:3) One lap a day. It's about the most relaxed battle plan ever written down.

The answer is that on the seventh day they circle the city seven times. Six days, one lap each. Then comes the seventh day: “…march around the city seven times, while the priests blow the horns.” (Joshua 6:4) Joshua 6:15 says that was the only day they circled seven times. Seven laps in one day? Somebody's getting their steps in.

The answers are shout and wall. The LORD says, “…have all the people give a mighty shout. Then the wall of the city will collapse and all your people will charge straight into the city.” (Joshua 6:5) Not a polite cheer, friends, but a mighty one, all the people together. It's the wall that comes down.

The answer is the rear guard. Picture a parade with the ark in the middle. The text says, “…the armed troops marched ahead of the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark.” (Joshua 6:9) Troops, priests, ark, then the rear guard. I bet that spot at the back had a great view of the whole line.

The answer is not one word until he says shout. Joshua commands the people, “Do not give a battle cry or let your voice be heard; do not let one word come out of your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then you are to shout!” (Joshua 6:10) The horns do the sounding. The people have to hold it all in until the day he says.

The answer is True. The text says, “So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. And the people returned to the camp and spent the night there.” (Joshua 6:11) One lap, then back to camp for the night. Then they got up and did it again the next day. That's some serious patience, and I know how hard waiting is. I once waited in a junk drawer for years.
The answer is False. On the second day, “…the horns kept sounding.” (Joshua 6:13) The priests keep blowing while they march. The people are the ones under orders to keep quiet.

The answer is dawn. The text says, “Then on the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times in the same manner.” (Joshua 6:15) It's an early start for a lot of laps. I'd be hitting snooze like it owed me money.

The answer is Rahab and all those with her. Joshua says, “Only Rahab the prostitute and all those with her in her house will live, because she hid the spies we sent.” (Joshua 6:17) The text gives her reason: she hid the spies. Everyone with her in her house is included. That's a house worth being in.
The answer is hid. Joshua says Rahab lives “…because she hid the spies we sent.” (Joshua 6:17) The text gives that as her reason. She hid them, and she and her house are spared.

The answer is False. No souvenirs, friends. Joshua says, “…all the silver and gold and all the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they must go into His treasury.” (Joshua 6:19) He also warns, “…keep away from the things devoted to destruction…” (Joshua 6:18)

The answer is the two men who spied out the land. Joshua tells “…the two men who had spied out the land…” to go into the house of the prostitute and bring out the woman and all who are with her. (Joshua 6:22) His words even include “…just as you promised her.” So the text shows the spies getting the job, and a promise to Rahab is part of the order. I think that fits nicely.

The answer is False. The spies do not settle Rahab's family inside the camp. Joshua 6:23 says the spies “…brought out her whole family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.” Outside the camp is where the text puts them. It adds nothing more about why.
The answer is Israelites. The text says, “So she has lived among the Israelites to this day.” (Joshua 6:25) Rahab ended up living with Israel. The writer says that was still true as he wrote.

The answer is that he is cursed before the LORD. Joshua says, “Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho…” (Joshua 6:26) That's a solemn oath. It's a serious one, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is True. Joshua says, “at the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundations; at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates.” (Joshua 6:26) The oath is about the man who rises up and rebuilds Jericho. This one is heavy, so I'll just let it stand as written.

The answer is True. The text says, “So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.” (Joshua 6:27) Both things sit in that one verse. Joshua's name got around the whole land. I think the part to hold onto is the first one, that the LORD was with him.
